name: SBMXG03-2024-7622
subject: Gear Lever Wiring (Cables) Solder Melting off.
outline:
In certain instances, Bobcat B70 machines may experience a critical issue where the gear lever wiring or cable can melt at the solder points, rendering the machine inoperable. This occurrence can prevent the engine from starting and compromise the overall functionality of the equipment.

The primary cause of this issue is the excessive heat generated during operation, leading to the deterioration of the solder connections in the gear lever wiring/cable assembly. The original 14-gauge cables may not effectively dissipate this heat, resulting in melting and subsequent failure.
implementation_procedure:
Items Required:
    Replacement 28-gauge thick cable
    Soldering iron with appropriate wattage
    Heat shrink tubing
    Wire strippers
    Screwdrivers
    Multi meter for testing

 Procedure:
 Ensure the machine is powered off and in a safe, stable position. Visually inspect the gear lever wiring and cable assembly for signs of melting or damage. Disconnect the machine from the power source. Identify the damaged section of the cable and carefully remove it using appropriate tools. Replace the original 14-gauge cable with the new 28-gauge cable, ensuring it is of sufficient length and compatible with the gear lever assembly. Strip the insulation from the ends of the new cable and the existing connections on the gear lever assembly. Use a soldering iron to securely solder the new cable to the gear lever assembly connections. Apply heat shrink tubing to cover the soldered joints, providing insulation and protection against further heat-related issues.

name: SBMXG05-2024-9330
subject: Air Conditioning Compressor Failures in Bobcat B730 Machines
outline: We have observed a pattern of AC compressor failures across multiple Bobcat B730 machines. This bulletin serves to notify you of this issue and provide guidance on how to check and maintain your machine to prevent potential failures.
implementation_procedure:
We advise all Bobcat B730 owners to perform a thorough check of their AC compressor to ensure it is functioning correctly. Please follow these steps to inspect your AC compressor:
•	Visual Inspection: Look for any visible signs of damage, leaks, or wear on the AC compressor and associated components.
•	Performance Test: Run the AC system and check if it cools the cabin effectively. Listen for any unusual noises coming from the compressor.
To avoid constant clutching of the AC compressor, which can lead to premature failure, we strongly advise the following operational practices:
•	Doors and Windows: Keep the doors and windows closed while operating the AC. Open doors and windows can cause the AC system to work harder, leading to frequent clutch cycling and increased wear on the compressor.

name: SBMXG06-2024-9638
subject: Unsuitability of Vögele Pavers to Lay G1 Base Material
outline: Bitumen World is currently facing significant challenges with the Vogele paver in laying G1 base. They would like to know if Wirtgen offers a specialized machine specifically designed for this purpose. They are experiencing problems with their current Vögele paver that has a base screed, specifically with bearings seizing on the front conveyor and abnormal wear. Due to the aforementioned issues, it is not viable for them to continue using the paver to lay G1 base. The customer has reported spending excessive amounts on parts and facing considerable downtime. As a temporary measure, they have reverted to using graders with GPS for laying G1 base, but this is not their preferred long-term solution.
implementation_procedure: Does Wirtgen have a machine that is specifically designed for laying G1 base material?

name: SBMXG08-2025-17340
subject: Failing Rear Drive Motor & Coupling
outline:
We have observed premature failure of the rear displacement motor on multiple Hamm HC208 units operating below 1500 engine hours.

Failure Mode:

 - Observed Condition: Excessive spline wear on both the motor shaft and the  drive coupling that mates to the shaft

Effect: 
- Loss of drive , rendering the machine immobile

Preliminary Observations:

Wear appears accelerated and may be due to:
- Undersized or insufficiently hardened splines
- Poor spline engagement
implementation_procedure:
We request the following;

- OEM technical analysis and feedback

- Confirmation if this is a known issue or subject to recall/modification campaign

- Recommendations for revised maintenance, inspection, or part replacement intervals

subject: Track Tensioner Rotation – Greasing Point Inaccessible
outline:
With regards to the above mentioned models, the following has been observed:

The track tensioner is rotating, causing the grease nipple to shift out of position and become inaccessible for tensioning. The factory-installed stopper appears insufficient to hold the tensioner in place over time
implementation_procedure:
To be corrected during Pre-Delivery Inspection (PDI) as follows:


Split the tracks, Remove the idler assembly, Weld a suitable stopper to prevent future rotation, Reassemble the idler and tracks

Approx Cost: $600

name: SBMXG08-2025-17539
subject: Radiator Neck Failures on SFD30 Forklifts Below 1000 Hours
outline:
We have recorded multiple instances of radiator neck breakage on SFD30 forklifts operating at less than 1000 hours.

    Failure Mode: Cracking or breaking of the radiator inlet/outlet neck

    Effect: Coolant leakage, overheating risk, and unplanned machine downtime

    Warranty History: Failures have been successfully repaired under warranty on all reported units
implementation_procedure:
Request for OEM Action:

1. Confirm if this failure mode is known to the factory and if any design revisions or reinforced radiator assemblies have been implemented.

2. Provide technical guidance on whether there are preventative measures we can take during Pre-Delivery Inspection (PDI) to reduce failure risk.

name: SBMXG11-2025-19613

outline: It has been identified that the hydraulic lock solenoid connector may experience poor electrical contact due to the insulated section of the wire extending too far into the connector cavity. This prevents proper pin contact within the connector.
implementation_procedure: Strip the wire insulation slightly to ensure the conductive part is fully exposed for correct terminal contact.

name: SBMXG01-2026-21437
subject: Rear drive motor coupling failure
outline:
- There have been repeat failures (4) on the rear drive motor coupling on the Hamm HC208. 
- Investigations reveal that the splines on the coupling wear out prematurely, resulting in loss of drive on the rear axle. 
- From a technical perspective, we have observed that the coupling on the HC208 is a connection in contrast with the Hamm 3520 models, which have an oil-lubricated coupling.
implementation_procedure: - Our recommendation to prevent future failure is for the HC208 to adopt the lubricated coupling as on the Hamm 3520 variant.

name: SBMXG02-2026-21500
subject: Potential Water Ingress Risk – Shield Air Intake Assembly (Item 15)
outline:
The shield air intake assembly, identified as Item 15 in the attached illustration does not appear to incorporate a
sufficient or dedicated drainage provision to allow accumulated water to evacuate effectively. Under operating conditions involving heavy rainfall, machine washing, or water splash, moisture may collect within
this section of the air intake system.
If excessive water accumulates within the shield air intake assembly (Item 15), there is a risk that the collected
water may be drawn into the engine air intake tract. This condition may result in water entering the engine cylinders,
significantly increasing the likelihood of engine damage. Potential failure modes include hydro-lock, accelerated
internal corrosion, and catastrophic engine failure.
implementation_procedure:
It is recommended that BOBCAT review the current design of the shield air intake assembly (Item 15) and consider
incorporating an adequate drainage feature. This may include a dedicated drain hole, drain channel, or water trap configuration to prevent water accumulation.

name: SBMXG05-2026-24201
subject: EX1200-7 Hydraulic Main Pump Air Bleeding Execution and ConSite Mine Shot Registration Requirement
outline:
This Service Letter serves as a notification regarding the execution and documentation of hydraulic main pump air bleeding on EX1200-7 mining excavators.
Recent hydraulic main pump failures have been linked to insufficient or undocumented air bleeding during maintenance and component replacement. Proper air bleeding is essential to prevent cavitation, internal damage, and premature main pump failure.
implementation_procedure:
AIR BLEEDING IS REQUIRED WHENEVER AIR ENTERS THE HYDRAULIC SYSTEM:

1. Initial Assembly/ First machine start-up - Bleed main pump, Target Cylinder and all applicable components
 Required as part of the final checks during assembly or initial operation to purge air from newly filled circuits. Bleed main pump, target cylinders, and all applicable components (main pump, fan pump, pilot main pump, suction pipes, hoses, regulators, solenoids)

2. Hydraulic Oil Replacement - Bleed main pump
Required after the hydraulic oil has been drained and refilled. This procedure is typically scheduled at 4,000 operating hours and includes cleaning the suction filter.

3. System Run Dry/Drawn Air - Bleed main pump
Required after severe events like the tank emptying, major leaks, or accidental air ingestion. Bleed thoroughly before resuming normal operation.

4. Component Removal/Installation - Bleed main pump and Target Component
Required after removing and reinstalling any major hydraulic component (e.g., main pump, motor, cylinder, control valve, hoses) where oil has been disconnected or lost

ATTACHMENTS AND DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS

All hydraulic main pump air bleeding work should be:
• Performed at the mine site, with photos taken of each hose to clearly show oil discharge.
• Recorded using the ConSite Mine Shot mobile application immediately during the work.
• Uploaded and confirmed in M-Find history

Proper and accurate registration is essential to maintain traceability and avoid issues during claim review.

UPLOAD INSTRUCTIONS:

1. Open ConSite Mine Shot (Mobile App).
2. Navigate according to the machine details.
3. Go to the “Others” section and upload each photo one by one.
Photo Comments:
4. For each photo (showing oil flow from the plug
port), indicate which hose it corresponds to
(a, b, c, or d).
Include any additional comments if necessary.
Hose a
5. After uploading, complete the entry accordingly
and submit/link it to M-Find.
Click “Link to M-find system”

appears correctly in the M-Find history section
